headline: Approved an interdepartmental transfer in the 2026-2027 budget for the Finance Department, unanimously.
summary: Members approved a budget transfer for the Finance Department by a unanimous vote. Several submitted items were sent to committees, including Catalis to Public Safety and Eili’s to Human Services. Two new items, a motor vehicle transfer agreement and an agreement with AKRF, Inc. for Hamden Center traffic signals, were opened.
decisions: Approved an interdepartmental transfer in the 2026-2027 budget for the Finance Department, 0 opposed, 0 abstentions.
Referred the Eili’s submission to Human Services.
Referred the resolutions to Admin & Settlement.
Referred the Catalis submission to Public Safety.

plain_text:
TOWN OF HAMDEN, 
CONNECTICUT 
 
LEGISLATIVE COUNCIL 
OCTOBER 19, 2026 – 7PM 
MINUTES DRAFT 
 
 
Present - Katie Kiely, President 
Present - Sean Cardwell, Pro Tem 
Absent - Sarah Gallagher, Maj Leader 
Absent - Bob Anthony, Min Leader 
Present - Tasha Hunt, Majority Whip 
Present - Tom Figlar, Minority Whip 
Present - Maurine Crouch 
Present - Doug Foley 
Present  - Jeron Alston 
Present  - Abdul Osmanu 
Absent - Rhonda Caldwell 
Present - Grace Teodosio 
Present - Adrian Webber 
Present - Ted Stevens 
Present - Tameeka Parks  
1. MEETING CONVENES  
 
 
Call of the Meeting and Taking of The Roll 
President Kiely called the meeting to order at 7:06pm with the members noted above 
in attendance.  Council members Gallagher, Anthony and Caldwell were absent.  
      
 2. Pledge of Allegiance and Moment of Silence 
      
 3. Land Acknowledgment 
      
 4. Leadership Update – no submissions for Leadership Update – trunk or treat at Keefe 
There were no submissions for leadership update for this evening’s meeting. President 
Kiely mentioned the upcoming Trunk or Treat event at Keefe  
      
 5. Mayor's Report 
There was no Mayor’s report given this evening. 
      
 6. News and Announcements –  
President Kiely noted that we did not have additional news/announcements for this 
week. She mentioned the upcoming audit and school building committee meetings and 
that the Ordinance and Rules were coming along.  She said there would be a full 
presentation so the public and the administration can weigh-in. 
      
 7. Celebrations 
No updates for this evening. 
      
2. REPORTS OF DEPARTMENTS, BOARDS, COMMISSIONS, AND COUNCIL LIAISONS  
 1. Report of Finance Commission 
There was no update for this evening’s meeting  
      
 2. Report of the Board of Education –  
The BOE met last week, the School Building Committee and Special Ed funding were 
discussed.   
      
 3. Council Liaison Reports 
There was no report for this evening. 
 
School Building Committee Organizational Meeting - OCTOBER 22, 2026, 8pm 
Memorial Town Hall Conference Room 111.
Board of Education — Regular Meetings are Hybrid and held on the 2nd Tuesday 
of the month.  Recent Agendas & Minutes 
  
      
3. PUBLIC INPUT AND CORRESPONDENCE 
No members of the public came forward to make public comment.  
4.    CONSENT CALENDAR 
 
1.ORDER AUTHORIZING INTERDEPARTMENTAL TRANSFER 2026 - 2027 FISCAL 
YEAR BUDGET - FINANCE DEPARTMENT 
Motion: Cardwell 
Second: Parks 
Vote: All in favor, 0 opposed; 0 abstentions. 
 
  
  
   
5. ANNOUNCEMENT OF COMMUNICATION CALENDAR    
 1. Review of Items submitted for October/November  
KK read the Submission items 
• Town Clerk 
• Funding Request from Department 
• Eili’s – refereed to Human Services 
• Opioid Case Manager – not referred 
• Easement Abatement – pending referral 
• Puppies Behind Bars – Public Safety 
• Motor Vehicle Tax Refunds – Next LC Agenda 
• Fleet Proposal – not referred 
• Resolutions – Referred to Admin & Settlement 
• 6 Orders CDBG – awaiting referral chair and dept communication along with 
memo 
• 8 Orders CDBG – awaiting referral chair and dept communication along with 
memo 
• PW transfer – still need info  
• Catalis – referred to Public Safety 
  
      
6. REGULAR AGENDA DELIBERATION AND ACTION  
There were no items for this evening 
  
7. RECESS FOR STANDING COMMITTEES 
Motion to Recess: Cardwell  
Second: Foley  
 1. Convene Standing Committee Meetings 
      
 2. Committees Adjourn 
Resumption of Regular Meeting Agenda 
      
Motion to come out of recess – moved Cardwell, 2nd Foley.
Return to full council agenda.  President Kiely requested of the Chairs that the agenda 
for the IT and Civic Engagement, Public Works, and Human Services Committees roll 
into Legislative Council since there were no items for vote on their agendas.  
 
IT Committee: Chair Foley noted that quarterly reports from the Technology Commission 
and IT Department had been provided and invited the Technology Commission Chair to 
present an update. The Commission reported ongoing efforts to develop a Town AI 
policy and understand the limitations of MUNIS. The Commission also reported two 
regular and two youth vacancies and the designation of Justin Schnieder as its liaison. In 
response to a question, it was confirmed that work had begun on software consolidation 
in coordination with Justin. With no further questions, Chair Foley closed the discussion 
at 8:07 p.m. 
Public Works Committee: President Kiely reviewed the Boards/Commissions noted on 
the Public Works Agenda.  Chair Stevens did not have any additional business to add for 
this evening. 
Human Services Committee:  President Kiely reviewed the Boards/Commissions noted 
on the Human Services Agenda. 
3. Receipt of Committee Reports 
President Kiely accepted the reports from the Engineering and Public Safety Committee. She 
called for a motion to suspend the rules and add two items from their agendas to New Business. 
Motion: Hunt 
Second: Figlar 
Vote: (2/3rd required): 10 in favor: Kiely, Cardwell, Hunt, Figlar, Crouch, Alston, Osmanu, 
Teodosio, Webber, Parks.  0 Opposed, 1 Abstention (Foley).  Motion to suspend the rules 
passes. 
 
8
. 
NEW BUSINESS 
 
1. Item from Public Safety 
ORDER AUTHORIZING A MOTOR VEHICLE TRANSFER AGREEMENT
Motion to open the item: Figlar 
Second: Parks 
Vote: All in favor, 0 opposed, 0 abstentions 
 
2. Item from Engineering, Development, & Municipal Planning   
ORDER APPROVING AND AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR TO SIGN AN 
AGREEMENT WITH AKRF, INC. - HAMDEN CENTER TRAFFIC SIGNAL 
IMPROVEMENTS-PHASE 2 ROUTE 10 (DIXWELL AVE) 
Motion to open the item: Parks 
Second: Figlar 
Vote: All in favor, 0 opposed, 0 abstentions.   
 
9. UNFINISHED BUSINESS 
No unfinished business for this evening
10. ADJOURNMENT – 
President Kiely asked for a motion to adjourn. 
Motion: Parks 
Second: Foley 
 
The meeting was adjourned at 8:30pm.
